moments.action: In a police office the moustached detective leans over the seated young driver, forehead cut, and talks him down. The boy starts looking up at him and ends glaring back, arguing.
Now on his feet, the boy is nose to nose with the detective, who jabs a finger at his face. A uniformed deputy clamps a hand on his shoulder and the boy turns his eyes away.
A red-haired woman in a tiger-print top storms in swinging at the boy, then stands over him berating him. He stops answering and ends slumped in the chair, head down.
Wide of the office: the woman keeps a hand on the seated boy while she argues with the detective. His hard face softens into a smile at her; the boy sits apart, glancing off.
The two adults settle over the desk paperwork, the detective explaining with open hands. She puts a cigarette to her lips, he leans in with a lighter, and the argument turns into easy talk.
The woman smokes seated beside the boy, under a board reading CRASH SITE VEHICLE, bargaining with the detective over his head. The boy watches the deal being made, then drops his eyes.
Through the office glass, the station lobby: a blonde girl and a boy in a purple number 13 jersey being tended to. The young driver turns back from the window with a cold, set look.

Out in the corridor the boy waits against the wall with the deputy posted nearby. His mother comes off the phone to him; by the last shot they are face to face and he is taking the verdict in silence.
Extreme close-up on the boy's eyes flicking sideways, then the scene becomes an airliner cabin: he sits wedged between elderly Japanese passengers, scowling, already on the flight out.
